## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment. The OMG workflow is: **idea → issue → playable project.** If you believe software should start with a sentence instead of a sprint plan, [⭐ star the repository](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub) and try it.
**Built with GitHub Actions, OpenCode, shared skills, and unreasonable optimism.** 😏

- 2D pixel art (canvas rendering at low internal resolution, scaled with nearest neighbor, procedural pixel sprites)
- 1v1 duels vs AI
- Difficulty: Easy / Medium / Hard (maybe also "Nightmare"? user said easy or medium or hard)
- High VFX (particles, screen shake, flashes, trails, glow, chromatic-ish effects)
- Minimalist UI
- Video settings (resolution scale, particles, screen shake, bloom, FPS cap, fullscreen)
- Parry mechanic (timed block/parry, deflects and opens window)
- Magic system (spells: fireball, frost nova, arcane bolts? with mana/cooldowns)
- Skill points system (earn points, spend on skill tree: health, mana, parry window, spell damage, etc.)
- Progressive (run-based progression through stages/opponents, unlocks)

Build quality: need it to look genuinely good. Design plan:

Game concept: "PARALLAX DUEL"? "PRISM DUEL". Minimalist pixel-art arena, two duelists on floating platform with parallax starfield. Names: "SPELLBREAK" — good title for magic + parry. Tagline: "Parry. Cast. Ascend."

Game flow:
- Title screen with pixel logo, animated background, menu: DUEL / SKILLS / SETTINGS / HOW TO PLAY.
- Difficulty select.
- Combat: side-view 1v1 arena. Movement left/right, jump, crouch? Keep simple: move, jump, dash.
- Attacks: light slash (J / click), heavy (K), magic (1/2/3 spells), parry (L / right click or Shift), dash (Shift?).
- Enemy AI with patterns telegraphs.
- Player has HP, MP, stamina? Keep HP + mana + parry cooldown.
- Progressive: after win, gain skill points, next opponent stronger; between rounds skill screen. Lose -> retry. Save to localStorage: best stage, skill points, unlocked spells.
- Boss every 3? Opponents with distinct palettes and magic.

Controls for desktop and mobile touch. Mobile buttons.

Visuals:
- Low-res canvas: internal 480x270 or 512x288, scaled to fit. Pixel art rendering with crisp edges. UI overlays maybe HTML for menus (crisp, minimalist) but pixel font.
- Character sprites: procedural drawing on offscreen canvases at low-res, maybe 16x32 pixel figures with animation frames: idle bob, run, jump, slash, cast, parry, hurt. Drawing manually via pixel arrays? Could generate pixel-art knight/mage characters via code arrays. That's effort but doable. Alternatively draw with shapes snapped to pixels — minimalist silhouettes with glow rim; characters as cloaked duelists made of simple pixel geometry with flowing cloak and eyes. Animation via transforms and limb rects.

High VFX: particle system (sparks, embers, motes), slash arcs, magic circles, shockwaves, screen shake, hitstop, damage numbers, afterimages, bloom via additive glow (shadowBlur expensive at low res but fine), background parallax with stars/fog, ground reflections, vignette, scanlines optional, freeze frames, particle bursts.

- Vitality (+max HP)

- Parry Window (+frames)
- Arcane Power (+spell dmg)
- Blade (+melee dmg)
- Swiftness (+move speed / dash cooldown)

export class AudioEngine {
  constructor(settings) {
    this.settings = settings || {}
    this.ctx = null
    this.master = null
    this.sfxBus = null
    this.musicBus = null
    this.noiseBuffer = null
    this.mode = 'off'
    this.nextPad = 0
    this.nextPluck = 0
    this.chordIndex = 0
    this.intensity = 0
    this.enabled = true
    this._lastSfx = new Map()
  }

  unlock() {
    if (!this.enabled) return
    if (!this.ctx) {
      const AC = window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext
      if (!AC) { this.enabled = false; return }
      try {
        this.ctx = new AC()
        this.master = this.ctx.createGain()
        this.master.gain.value = this.settings.volume ?? 0.8
        this.master.connect(this.ctx.destination)
        this.sfxBus = this.ctx.createGain()
        this.sfxBus.gain.value = this.settings.sfx ?? 0.9
        this.sfxBus.connect(this.master)
        this.musicBus = this.ctx.createGain()
        this.musicBus.gain.value = (this.settings.music ?? 0.45) * 0.5
        this.musicBus.connect(this.master)
        this.noiseBuffer = this._makeNoise()
        this.nextPad = this.ctx.currentTime + 0.1
        this.nextPluck = this.ctx.currentTime + 1.2
      } catch {
        this.enabled = false
      }
    }
    if (this.ctx && this.ctx.state === 'suspended') this.ctx.resume().catch(() => {})
  }

  _makeNoise() {
    const ctx = this.ctx
    const length = Math.floor(ctx.sampleRate * 1.2)
    const buffer = ctx.createBuffer(1, length, ctx.sampleRate)
    const data = buffer.getChannelData(0)
    for (let i = 0; i < length; i++) data[i] = Math.random() * 2 - 1
    return buffer
  }

  setSettings(settings) {
    this.settings = settings
    if (!this.ctx) return
    const t = this.ctx.currentTime
    this.master.gain.setTargetAtTime(settings.volume ?? 0.8, t, 0.03)
    this.sfxBus.gain.setTargetAtTime(settings.sfx ?? 0.9, t, 0.03)
    this.musicBus.gain.setTargetAtTime((settings.music ?? 0.45) * 0.5, t, 0.05)
  }

  setMode(mode) {
    if (mode === this.mode) return
    this.mode = mode
    if (!this.ctx) return
    this.chordIndex = 0
    this.nextPad = this.ctx.currentTime + 0.05
    this.nextPluck = this.ctx.currentTime + 0.8
  }

  setIntensity(value) {
    this.intensity = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, value))
  }

  _tone({ freq = 440, end = freq, dur = 0.15, type = 'sine', gain = 0.12, attack = 0.005, release = 0.12, pan = 0, filter = 0, filterEnd = filter, bus = null }) {
    if (!this.ctx) return
    const ctx = this.ctx
    const t = ctx.currentTime
    const osc = ctx.createOscillator()
    const env = ctx.createGain()
    const panner = ctx.createStereoPanner ? ctx.createStereoPanner() : null
    osc.type = type
    osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(Math.max(20, freq), t)
    osc.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(Math.max(20, end), t + dur)
    env.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, t)
    env.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(Math.max(0.0002, gain), t + attack)
    env.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + dur + release)
    let node = osc
    if (filter) {
      const biquad = ctx.createBiquadFilter()
      biquad.type = 'lowpass'
      biquad.frequency.setValueAtTime(filter, t)
      biquad.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(Math.max(60, filterEnd), t + dur)
      biquad.Q.value = 2
      node.connect(biquad)
      node = biquad
    }
    if (panner) {
      panner.pan.value = pan
      node.connect(panner)
      node = panner
    }
    node.connect(env)
    env.connect(bus || this.sfxBus)
    osc.start(t)
    osc.stop(t + dur + release + 0.05)
  }

  _noise({ dur = 0.15, gain = 0.12, filter = 1400, filterEnd = filter, type = 'bandpass', q = 0.8, pan = 0, bus = null, delay = 0 }) {
    if (!this.ctx || !this.noiseBuffer) return
    const ctx = this.ctx
    const t = ctx.currentTime + delay
    const src = ctx.createBufferSource()
    src.buffer = this.noiseBuffer
    const biquad = ctx.createBiquadFilter()
    biquad.type = type
    biquad.frequency.setValueAtTime(filter, t)
    biquad.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(Math.max(50, filterEnd), t + dur)
    biquad.Q.value = q
    const env = ctx.createGain()
    env.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, t)
    env.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(Math.max(0.0002, gain), t + 0.008)
    env.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + dur)
    const panner = ctx.createStereoPanner ? ctx.createStereoPanner() : null
    src.connect(biquad)
    if (panner) {
      panner.pan.value = pan
      biquad.connect(panner)
      panner.connect(env)
    } else {
      biquad.connect(env)
    }
    env.connect(bus || this.sfxBus)
    src.start(t)
    src.stop(t + dur + 0.02)
  }

  play(name, { pitch = 1, gain = 1, pan = 0 } = {}) {
    if (!this.ctx || !this.settings.sfx) return
    const now = this.ctx.currentTime
    const last = this._lastSfx.get(name) || 0
    if (now - last < 0.018) return

    const ctx = this.ctx
    const t = ctx.currentTime
    const env = ctx.createGain()
    env.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, t)
    env.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(gain, t + 1.2)
    env.gain.setValueAtTime(gain, t + dur - 0.6)
    env.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + dur)
    const filter = ctx.createBiquadFilter()
    filter.type = 'lowpass'
    filter.frequency.value = 900 + this.intensity * 1600
    filter.Q.value = 0.6
    filter.connect(env)
    env.connect(bus || this.musicBus)
    freqs.forEach((freq, i) => {
      const osc = ctx.createOscillator()
      osc.type = i === 0 ? 'triangle' : 'sine'
      osc.frequency.value = freq
      osc.detune.value = (i - 1) * 5
      const vg = ctx.createGain()
      vg.gain.value = i === 0 ? 0.5 : 0.28
      osc.connect(vg)
      vg.connect(filter)
      osc.start(t)
      osc.stop(t + dur + 0.1)
    })
  }

  _pluck(freq) {
    if (!this.ctx) return
    const ctx = this.ctx
    const t = ctx.currentTime
    const osc = ctx.createOscillator()
    const env = ctx.createGain()
    osc.type = 'sine'
    osc.frequency.value = freq
    env.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, t)
    env.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.022, t + 0.01)
    env.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + 0.9)
    osc.connect(env)
    env.connect(this.musicBus)
    osc.start(t)
    osc.stop(t + 0.95)
  }

  update() {
    if (!this.ctx || !this.settings.music || this.mode === 'off' || this.ctx.state !== 'running') return
    const t = this.ctx.currentTime
    if (this.nextPad < t + 0.2) {
      const menuChords = [
        [NOTE.C2, NOTE.G2, NOTE.E3, NOTE.B3],
        [NOTE.A2, NOTE.E3, NOTE.C4, NOTE.G4],
        [NOTE.F2, NOTE.C3, NOTE.A3, NOTE.E4],
        [NOTE.G2, NOTE.D3, NOTE.B3, NOTE.F4],
      ]
      const fightChords = [
        [NOTE.D2, NOTE.A2, NOTE.F3, NOTE.C4],
        [NOTE.B2, NOTE.F3, NOTE.D4, NOTE.A4],
        [NOTE.G2, NOTE.D3, NOTE.B3, NOTE.F4],
        [NOTE.A2, NOTE.E3, NOTE.C4, NOTE.G4],
      ]
      const bossChords = [
        [NOTE.C2, NOTE.G2, NOTE.E3, NOTE.A3],
        [NOTE.A2, NOTE.E3, NOTE.C4, NOTE.F4],
        [NOTE.F2, NOTE.C3, NOTE.A3, NOTE.D4],
        [NOTE.G2, NOTE.D3, NOTE.B3, NOTE.E4],
      ]
      const chords = this.mode === 'boss' ? bossChords : this.mode === 'fight' ? fightChords : menuChords
      const chord = chords[this.chordIndex % chords.length]
      this.chordIndex++
      const dur = this.mode === 'menu' ? 6.4 : 3.6
      this._pad(chord, dur + 0.6, this.mode === 'menu' ? 0.075 : 0.085)
      this._pad([chord[0] / 2], dur + 0.4, 0.09)
      this.nextPad = t + dur
    }
    if (this.nextPluck < t + 0.1) {
      const scale = this.mode === 'menu'
        ? [NOTE.E4, NOTE.G4, NOTE.A4, NOTE.C5, NOTE.B4, NOTE.G4]
        : [NOTE.A4, NOTE.C5, NOTE.E5, NOTE.D5, NOTE.G5, NOTE.E5, NOTE.C5, NOTE.D5]
      const note = scale[Math.floor(Math.random() * scale.length)]
      if (Math.random() < 0.72) this._pluck(note)
      const pace = this.mode === 'menu' ? 1.9 : this.mode === 'boss' ? 0.7 : 1.0
      this.nextPluck = t + pace * (0.7 + Math.random() * 0.8)
    }
  }
}

## Objective
- Build a playable browser game from the user's brief: "2d, pixil ART, 1v1, Eazy or medium or hard, HIGH VFX, minimalist, vídeo settings, parry, magics, skill points sistem, progressive".
- The assistant chose to build "SPELLBREAK": a minimalist pixel-art 1v1 magic/parry duel with difficulty selection, video settings, spells, a persistent skill tree, and ten-stage progressive ascent.

## Requirements
- 2D pixel art, minimalist visual style, high VFX.
- 1v1 duels against AI with Easy / Medium / Hard difficulty.
- Video settings menu.
- Parry mechanic, magic/spell combat.
- Skill-point progression system that persists and unlocks over stages.
- Progressive stage/opponent structure.
- Must run as a static site (`index.html` served directly; no build step expected).

## Decisions
- Vanilla JS ES modules + HTML Canvas, no framework/build tool; static server compatible.
- Procedural pixel-art fighters/background rendered at low internal resolution and upscaled with `image-rendering: pixelated`.
- 10 handcrafted stages then endless "ascension" scaling; two boss gates (stages 5 and 10).
- Spells: `ember` (projectile, unlock stage 1), `frost` (AOE slow, stage 3), `storm` (delayed lightning, stage 5).
- Skill tree: 8 nodes with rank costs; points persist in `localStorage` under `spellbreak.save.v1`.
- Difficulty rewards: Easy +2 SP, Medium +3 SP, Hard +4 SP; first-clear boss bonus +2 SP.
- Added local pixel font files downloaded from Google Fonts: Silkscreen 400/700 WOFF2 in `assets/`.
- HUD is DOM-based; in-world effects/text are canvas-based.
- Includes synthesized WebAudio SFX/music (no audio assets), touch controls, fullscreen, scanlines, reduced flashes/motion.

## Work State
### Completed
- Wrote `src/config.js` with arena/physics constants, attacks, parry/dash, spells, difficulties, 10 stages, palettes, skills, derived stats, spell unlocks, endless stage scaling.
- Wrote `src/save.js` with save sanitization/defaults/settings (including `reduceMotion`, `highestCleared`).
- Wrote `src/input.js` with keyboard mapping and touch/edge input.
- Wrote `src/audio.js` with synthesized SFX, music scheduler, volume handling; added `delay` support to `_tone`.
- Wrote `src/fx.js` with particle/ring/arc/sigil/bolt/text/flash systems, trauma shake, hitstop, slow-motion, ghosts, quality scaling.
- Wrote `src/sprites.js` with parallax sky/moon/mountains/platform/runes and procedural fighter rendering, ghost rendering, blade trails, vignette.
- Wrote `src/fighter.js` with movement, combos, heavy breaker, parry, dash, casting, guard, hit reactions, statuses, death, and AI.
- Wrote `src/game.js` with camera, projectiles, storm sigils, hit resolution, parry/reflect, boss phase, HUD data, attract mode, render pipeline, FPS cap accumulator.
- Wrote `index.html` with title, difficulty, skill tree, settings, help, VS, result, pause screens, HUD, spell bar, touch controls, toast/combo.
- Wrote `styles.css` with full responsive minimalist UI, pixel font, title/menu screens, HUD, skill board, settings/toggles/sliders, touch layout, scanlines/reduce-motion.
- Wrote `src/main.js` with screen orchestration, save integration, difficulty flow, stage/VS flow, results/rewards, skill purchasing/refunds, settings binding, pause/restart/quit, touch/keyboard bindings, QA hook `window.__spellbreak`.
- Downloaded font assets `assets/silkscreen-400.woff2`, `assets/silkscreen-700.woff2`.
- Ran `node --check` successfully on all JS modules at last check.

### Active
- Need to run the game in a browser, fix runtime/visual bugs, and capture screenshots for verification.
- Need to add remaining CSS for `.node-cost` (referenced in `main.js` but not yet styled).
- Need to verify font files load correctly with static server MIME (`application/octet-stream`); fallback is monospace if not.
- Need to validate gameplay balance/AI and all screen flows end-to-end.

### Blocked
- None known.

## Next Move
1. Start the static server (e.g., `PORT=3002 node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs"`) and open `http://localhost:3002`.
2. Use `playwright-cli` to check console/page errors, font loading, title/difficulty/gameplay/skills/settings screens.
3. Fix discovered runtime bugs; particularly inspect `src/game.js` render order, camera, hit detection, AI parry/cast behavior, victory/defeat flow, pause flow.
4. Add `.node-cost` CSS and any missing responsive fixes.
5. Play through stage 1 on each difficulty via `window.__spellbreak`/inputs; confirm parry, spells, combo, SP rewards, stage advancement, skill purchases, and spell unlocks.
6. Capture desktop and mobile screenshots into `screenshots/`, inspect them, and iterate until visuals and gameplay are solid.
7. Optionally add a lightweight smoke test and update `README.md` with game/controls info; commit final state.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: UI flow, save orchestration, screen bindings, QA hook.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: core match loop, camera, projectiles, results events.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/fighter.js`: combat state machine and enemy AI.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/sprites.js`: all procedural visuals.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM screens/HUD/touch structure.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: complete visual design/responsive rules.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/config.js`: balance data, stages, skills, spells.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/fx.js`: VFX/particles/shake/hitstop.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: synthesized audio.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/save.js`: persistence/settings schema.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/input.js`: keyboard/touch input.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/assets/`: Silkscreen WOFF2 fonts.

## Important Context
- Working directory is the repo root; `start.sh`/`capture.sh` invoke runtime scripts and need `RUNTIME_DIR`; default start serves static `index.html` and supports `.html/.js/.css/.png` but not explicitly `.woff2` MIME.
- `default-capture.mjs` auto-clicks a button whose aria-label/text is exactly "Play"/"Start"/"Play Game"; `#btn-play` has `aria-label="Play"`, so fresh-save capture lands on the difficulty screen.
- `localStorage` key: `spellbreak.save.v1`; defaults include `points: 3`.
- Save progression: `save.stage` is 0-based next stage; `save.highestStage` is highest stage number reached (spell unlocks use it); `save.highestCleared` gates first-clear rewards.
- Spell unlocks rely on `save.highestStage`; clearing stage 2 should set highestStage to 3 and unlock Frost; stage 4 clear should unlock Storm.
- `window.__spellbreak` exposes `game`, `save` getter, `startStage`, `skipVS`, `play`, `openSkills`, `openSettings`, `showScreen`, `chooseDifficulty`, `beginAscent`, `pauseGame`, `resumeGame`, `refresh`.
- No `package.json` should be added unless choosing Vite; `default-start.mjs` rejects a package project without Vite.
- Screenshots directory is gitignored (`screenshots/`).
- No commits have been made yet for the new game files.

import {
  ARENA, PHYSICS, SPELLS, PALETTES, DIFFICULTIES, stageFor, SPELL_ORDER, MAX_HP_TRAIL,
} from './config.js'
import { Fighter } from './fighter.js'
import { drawSky, drawPlatform, drawFighter, drawGhost, drawBladeTrail, drawVignette, drawConfetti, hexA } from './sprites.js'
import { FX } from './fx.js'

const TAU = Math.PI * 2
const clamp = (v, a, b) => Math.max(a, Math.min(b, v))
const lerp = (a, b, t) => a + (b - a) * t
const rand = (a, b) => a + Math.random() * (b - a)
const sign = v => (v >= 0 ? 1 : -1)

export class Camera {
  constructor() {
    this.width = 480
    this.height = 300
    this.viewW = 440
    this.scale = 1.1
    this.x = 0
    this.groundScreen = 220
    this.groundFrac = 0.75
    this.shakeX = 0
    this.shakeY = 0
    this.punch = 0
    this.baseScale = 1.1
  }

  configure(width, height, viewW, groundFrac) {
    this.width = width
    this.height = height
    this.viewW = viewW
    this.groundFrac = groundFrac
    this.scale = width / viewW
    this.baseScale = this.scale
    this.groundScreen = height * groundFrac
  }

  X(x) { return (x - this.x) * this.scale + this.width / 2 + this.shakeX }
  Y(y) { return this.groundScreen + y * this.scale + this.shakeY }
  S(v) { return v * this.scale }

  clampX(x) {
    const half = this.viewW / 2
    const min = -ARENA.halfWidth + half - 12
    const max = ARENA.halfWidth - half + 12
    if (min > max) return 0
    return clamp(x, min, max)
  }
}

class Projectile {
  constructor({ owner, type, x, y, vx, vy, dmg, game }) {
    this.owner = owner
    this.type = type
    this.x = x
    this.y = y
    this.vx = vx
    this.vy = vy
    this.dmg = dmg
    this.radius = SPELLS[type]?.radius || 5
    this.life = 2.4
    this.dead = false
    this.color = SPELLS[type]?.color || '#ff8a3c'
    this.glow = SPELLS[type]?.glow || '#ffb35c'
    this.trail = 0
    this.reflected = false
    this.spin = 0
    this.game = game
  }

  update(dt, game) {
    if (this.dead) return
    this.life -= dt
    if (this.life <= 0) { this.dead = true; return }
    this.x += this.vx * dt
    this.y += this.vy * dt
    this.spin += dt * 14
    this.trail -= dt
    if (this.trail <= 0) {
      this.trail = 0.018
      const c = this.reflected ? this.owner.palette.trim : this.color
      game.fx.particle({
        x: this.x - this.vx * 0.01, y: this.y + rand(-1.5, 1.5),
        vx: -this.vx * 0.12 + rand(-12, 12), vy: rand(-18, 18),
        life: 0.32, size: 2.2, color: c, glow: true, drag: 2.6, gravity: -20,
      })
      game.fx.particle({
        x: this.x, y: this.y, vx: rand(-30, 30), vy: rand(-30, 10),
        life: 0.22, size: 1.2, color: '#ffffff', glow: true, drag: 2,
      })
    }
    if (this.y > 4) { this.dead = true; game.fx.burst(this.x, 0, { count: 8, colors: [this.color, '#ffffff'], speed: 70, life: 0.3, gravity: 150 }); return }

    const target = this.owner === game.player ? game.enemy : game.player
    if (!target || target.dead) return
    const dx = this.x - target.x
    const bodyTop = target.y - 34
    if (Math.abs(dx) < 10 + this.radius && this.y > bodyTop - 8 && this.y < target.y + 4) {
      if (target.parryActive && target.isParryingFrom(this.owner)) {
        game.resolveParry(target, this.owner, this)
        this.reflected = true
        this.owner = target
        this.vx *= -1.35
        this.vy = -18
        this.dmg *= 1.45
        this.color = target.palette.trim
        this.glow = target.palette.accent
        this.life = Math.max(this.life, 1.4)
        this.radius += 1
        return
      }
      const result = target.takeHit({
        dmg: this.dmg, kb: 95, guardBreak: false, hitstop: 0.06, shake: 0.28,
        name: 'SPELL',
      }, this.owner, game)
      game.resolveHitResult(this.owner, target, this.dmg, result, { spell: this.type, x: this.x, y: this.y })
      this.dead = true
      if (result === 'hit') {
        target.burnT = Math.max(target.burnT || 0, 1.5)
      }
    }
  }

  render(ctx, cam) {
    const x = cam.X(this.x)
    const y = cam.Y(this.y)
    const s = cam.scale
    const r = this.radius * s
    ctx.save()
    ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'
    const g = ctx.createRadialGradient(x, y, 0, x, y, r * 3.2)
    g.addColorStop(0, hexA(this.glow, 0.8))
    g.addColorStop(0.45, hexA(this.color, 0.35))
    g.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(0,0,0,0)')
    ctx.fillStyle = g
    ctx.fillRect(x - r * 3.2, y - r * 3.2, r * 6.4, r * 6.4)
    ctx.fillStyle = this.color
    ctx.beginPath()
    ctx.arc(x, y, r, 0, TAU)
    ctx.fill()
    ctx.fillStyle = '#ffffff'
    ctx.beginPath()
    ctx.arc(x - this.vx * 0.002 * s, y, r * 0.45, 0, TAU)
    ctx.fill()
    // trailing shard
    for (let i = 1; i <= 4; i++) {
      const tx = x - this.vx * 0.0035 * s * i
      const ty = y - this.vy * 0.0035 * s * i
      ctx.globalAlpha = 0.4 - i * 0.08
      ctx.fillStyle = this.glow
      ctx.fillRect(tx - r * 0.3, ty - r * 0.3, r * 0.6, r * 0.6)
    }
    ctx.restore()
  }
}

  resize() {
    const rect = this.canvas.getBoundingClientRect()
    const dpr = Math.min(2, window.devicePixelRatio || 1)
    const displayW = Math.max(320, rect.width || window.innerWidth)
    const displayH = Math.max(240, rect.height || window.innerHeight)
    const portrait = displayH > displayW * 1.15
    const touch = matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)').matches || navigator.maxTouchPoints > 0
    const res = this.settings.resolution
    let cssPerPixel = touch ? 2.1 : 3.1
    if (res === 'sharp') cssPerPixel = touch ? 1.6 : 2.2
    else if (res === 'balanced') cssPerPixel = touch ? 2.1 : 3.1
    else if (res === 'chunky') cssPerPixel = touch ? 2.7 : 4.2
    // keep the backing store manageable on huge displays
    const targetW = Math.min(displayW / cssPerPixel, 760)
    const scale = displayW / targetW
    const internalW = Math.max(180, Math.round(displayW / scale))
    const internalH = Math.max(140, Math.round(internalW * displayH / displayW))
    if (this.canvas.width !== internalW || this.canvas.height !== internalH) {
      this.canvas.width = internalW
      this.canvas.height = internalH
    }
    this.display = { width: displayW, height: displayH, portrait, touch, dpr }
    let viewW
    if (portrait) viewW = clamp(displayW / 2.65, 138, 205)
    else if (touch && displayH < 520) viewW = clamp(displayW / 2.75, 300, 430)
    else viewW = clamp(displayW / 3.2, 320, 470)
    const groundFrac = portrait ? 0.76 : 0.75
    this.cam.configure(internalW, internalH, viewW, groundFrac)
    this.cam.scale = internalW / viewW
    this.ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false
    this.fx.setQuality(this.settings.effects)
    this.fx.glow = this.settings.glow

The body drawing calls `pline(ctx, L(...), V(...), L(...), V(...), width, color)`. That's **8 arguments** instead of 7! Because each point requires two coords: x1, y1, x2, y2, width, color. They are passing L1, V1, L2, V2, ..., that's correct actually: `pline(ctx, L(...), V(...), L(...), V(...), width, color)` = ctx + 4 coords + width + color = 7 args. Yes that's fine. Wait look at line 466: pline(ctx, L(shoulder[0], V(shoulder[1])), L(-2 + walk, V(-21)), ...). Hmm L takes (x,y) but both args: x and y. L ignores its second arg. The pattern seems the author confused L(x, V(y)) as a point. But arguments are L(...) returning x, then L(...) again returning x, so `pline(ctx, x1, x2, ...)` missing y coords! That's why body invisible: all body line drawing passes only 3 arguments after ctx: Lx, Lx, width, color. Wait line 466:

`pline(ctx, L(shoulder[0], V(shoulder[1])), L(-2 + walk, V(-21)), Math.max(1.4, 2.1 * s), color('cloakDark'))`

Arguments after ctx: L(...) → x1, L(...) → y1 (actually second x), Math.max(...) → x2! width→y2, color→width, color undefined → color. That's broken. Plines draw garbage from x2=width (1-2px) etc off-canvas. That's why only shadow ellipse visible.

So drawFighter body uses incorrect call convention: L(x,y) is intended point but returns x only. The author probably meant a helper point, or use L(x, y) to get x and V(y) for y. Need fix all pline calls to pass x and y separately. E.g. `pline(ctx, L(shoulder[0],0), V(shoulder[1]), L(-2+walk,0), V(-21), width, color)`.

That's a lot of calls. Better redefine L to return a point? But L is used in px calls as x coordinate: `px(ctx, L(cx - half, V(y)), width, height, color)` — px expects x, y, w, h, color: here L returns x, V returns y, width, height, color = correct. So px calls are correct (L gives x, V gives y). pline calls incorrectly embed V inside L argument instead of as separate argument. Let's search all `pline(` lines and fix.
